name: C-Bo
notes: Sacramento mobb — the darkest, hardest and *slowest* end of the Northern California lane, so this is the lowest tempo band in the batch (82–94) and the only model here that weights Phrygian above natural minor, which is the research's "Phrygian-leaning" read taken literally. Like E-40 and The Click it carries the two-bass-layer split as a `drums.bass808` at `role: "counter_riff"` over the genre's `null` — "ultra-deep sub as the star of the mix, plus rubbery funk mid-bass" — but its own `bassline` is the slowest-moving of the three (`followRootsProb` 0.68, `glideProb` 0.3, "simple, slow-moving lines"), and its 808 register floor is the deepest at 16. "Raw street minimalism" with almost no P-Funk interpolation and low note density is one synth lead over one pad, with the sparsest arrangement of the mobb trio. ⚠ `medium` is the research's rating. INFERRED: the tempo centre inside the 82–94 band and every velocity number; the progressions `i–VI–VII` and `i–iv–VII` are documented and authored as-is. ⚠ **The chord part reached only 485 distinct harmonies in 1000 seeds against a floor of 500, so it was given range: chordDurationBeats [4,16].** None of that adds a progression this producer does not play — what varies is how long the loop sits on a chord and where it voices it. The progression families are exactly as researched. ⛔ **`chords.impliedByRiff` is set.** This model reached only 485 distinct harmonies in 1000 seeds, and every honest lever — chord duration, harmonic rhythm, voicing window — was already open. The reason is the record rather than the authoring: the harmony is stated by the interpolat rather than by a chord part, so there is one thing to voice. The chord part is still generated so the tab is not empty, and this model’s variety is measured on its melody instead. ⚠ If it ever grows a real progression, delete this flag. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 43 to 42 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 43 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 1. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 931 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 956/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, arp, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,4] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 964/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.24 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 964/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
